framework.name: next
framework.notes: App Router only (no pages dir). Next 16 conventions: the middleware file is src/proxy.ts (not middleware.ts) and it composes Arcjet + clerkMiddleware + next-intl routing. React 19.2.8; reactCompiler enabled for production builds (next.config.ts). next-intl plugin + withSentryConfig wrappers in next.config.ts. An extra runtime dep, translation-resilience (0.3.0), installs a client DOM shim from src/instrumentation-client.ts so browser auto-translation cannot break React updates.

monorepo.notes: Single root package.json; only package-lock.json present (pnpm-lock.yaml / yarn.lock / bun.lock all 404); CI installs with `npm ci`.

auth.notes: Clerk only (@clerk/nextjs 7.5.12). src/proxy.ts protects /dashboard(.*) via createRouteMatcher; UI comes from Clerk-hosted components on catch-all routes (SignIn/SignUp/UserProfile); ClerkProvider is mounted in the (auth) layout with cssLayerName 'clerk' for Tailwind 4. README claims passkeys/MFA/social/impersonation - that is Clerk dashboard config, not repo code. No role, permission or tenant code exists anywhere in the tree.

env.notes: Names only - no values read or recorded. Env.ts (T3 Env + zod) validates 11 vars; the three in required_at_build are z.string().min(1) so they are mandatory, and next.config.ts does `import './src/libs/Env'` at module load, so `next build`/`next dev` abort without them. ARCJET_KEY, the Sentry vars, Better Stack vars and both PostHog vars are .optional() and their features silently switch off when unset. NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DISABLED / NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED / BROWSER_TO_TERMINAL_DISABLED / SENTRY_ORGANIZATION / SENTRY_PROJECT / SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN / CHECKLY_* / PORT are read with raw process.env (next.config.ts, src/instrumentation*.ts, playwright.config.ts). CI-only secrets, never read by the app: CODECOV_TOKEN, CHROMATIC_PROJECT_TOKEN, CROWDIN_PROJECT_ID, CROWDIN_PERSONAL_TOKEN, CHECKLY_API_KEY, CHECKLY_ACCOUNT_ID.

deploy.notes: No Dockerfile, docker-compose, vercel.json or netlify.toml anywhere in the tree (Dockerfile -> 404 on main). README deploy section is platform-agnostic: define DATABASE_URL + CLERK_SECRET_KEY, `npm run build`, `npm run start`; migrations run automatically inside the build (build = run-s db:migrate build:next). `npm run build-local` builds against a throwaway in-memory PGLite server and needs no external DB. next.config.ts sets no `output: 'standalone'` (only outputFileTracingIncludes for ./migrations on '/'). Soft Vercel hints only: .gitignore ignores .vercel and the proxy matcher excludes /_vercel. CI runs unit/e2e jobs inside mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.62.1 containers - that is a test runner, not a deploy image.

tests.notes: unit_files = src/templates/BaseTemplate.test.tsx + src/utils/Helpers.test.ts. vitest.config.ts defines two projects: 'unit' (node env, src/**/*.test.ts) and 'ui' (*.test.tsx + src/hooks/**/*.test.ts in headless chromium via vitest browser mode + Playwright). e2e_files = tests/e2e/{Counter,I18n,Sanity.check,Visual}.e2e.ts; there is also 1 integration file (tests/integration/Counter.integ.ts) which Playwright, not vitest, runs (testMatch '*.(integ|e2e).ts'). Storybook 10 + 1 story file, tested with `npm run storybook:test`. CI.yml jobs: build, static (commitlint + next typegen + oxlint + knip + i18n-check), unit (+Codecov), storybook, e2e (+Chromatic visual regression; chromium locally, chromium+firefox in CI). Sanity.check.e2e.ts is consumed by Checkly, not by CI. package.json scripts: test, test:e2e, storybook:test, check:types, check:deps, check:i18n, lint.

pitfalls.detail: CLERK_SECRET_KEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY and DATABASE_URL are z.string().min(1) and next.config.ts imports src/libs/Env at module load, so dev AND build abort instantly without them; the tracked .env ships placeholder values only (a Clerk *test* publishable key plus 'your_clerk_secret_key'), so the app cannot run until you create a Clerk app and a database

`npm run build` = run-s db:migrate build:next, so a production build requires a REACHABLE Postgres - a wrong DATABASE_URL makes the Next build hang ~60s and fail; use `npm run build-local` (throwaway in-memory PGLite) for offline/CI builds

The dev database is PGLite served over a socket by @electric-sql/pglite-socket (`db-server:file` creates local.db and runs migrations first) - no Docker and no external Postgres are needed, but a bare `next dev` has no database: always start through `npm run dev`
README 'Checkly monitoring' tells you to update `checkly.config.ts` - that file does not exist on main (404); Checkly is only a sponsor logo, three env names and the *.check.e2e.ts naming convention

README feature list and the marketing page still advertise 'Analytics with PostHog', 'ESLint, Prettier' and 'Husky, Commitlint', but package.json contains no posthog, eslint, prettier or husky - lint/format run through oxlint+oxfmt via ultracite and hooks through lefthook. The two PostHog env vars are validated in Env.ts yet no PostHog SDK or init code exists

AGENTS.md (the agent instruction file that CLAUDE.md imports) says 'Only these bun run scripts' and 'Follow existing ESLint setup', but the repo ships package-lock.json and CI runs `npm ci` - there is no bun lockfile, so following its commands literally leads nowhere

Promotional copy for the author's paid Pro/Plus kits is baked into the app itself (Dashboard locale strings + src/components/Hello.tsx + the sponsor table), so a rebranded product still markets someone else's products on /dashboard

/portfolio, /portfolio/0../portfolio/5, /about and /counter are pure demo pages (placeholder paragraphs, a counter table, sponsor wall); the fixed DemoBadge is injected into the root layout so it renders on every page until deleted

package.json pins `overrides: { hono: 4.12.31 }` for a dependency that is only transitive (via Clerk/Arcjet) - bumping those packages may silently fight the override, and dependency tooling (knip / npm ls) will not explain it

Unit tests are not plain node tests: the vitest 'ui' project runs *.test.tsx in headless chromium (vitest browser mode + Playwright) and CI executes test jobs inside mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.62.1, so locally `npx playwright install` is needed before `npm run test` succeeds

.env and .env.production ARE tracked in git (only *.local is gitignored), so an agent tempted to 'just drop secrets in .env' would commit them; the repo convention is .env.local / .env.production.local

verdict.best_for: A new Next.js 16 App Router product that needs the boring plumbing done and nothing else: real auth with hosted UI, Postgres+Drizzle with migrations wired into the build, two-locale i18n, a full unit/integration/e2e/Storybook harness and a CI pipeline that works on day one.
verdict.weak_for: Anything SaaS-shaped beyond accounts - no billing/Stripe, no teams, roles or permissions, no email, uploads, admin panel, analytics or API keys; the paid Pro/Plus sibling kits are where those live.
verdict.swap_burden: light - no Dockerfile and almost no proprietary lock-in (Clerk is the only deep one, 3-5 days to replace), so the real work is deleting the sponsor/demo surface and adding your own UI kit and features.

unmeasured: Exact line counts per file: loc_estimate 2084 is derived from blob byte sizes (72,953 B / 35 B-per-line sampled on 10 files), not a true count of all 63 source files.
Runtime behaviour: nothing was cloned or executed (contract rule), so 'the demo works' is inferred from source and CI config only.
Actual test coverage %, CI pass/fail history and Codecov numbers (would need a Codecov account/token); only the CI job list from CI.yml was read.

OpenGraph/Twitter metadata: two open issues and one open PR request it; I found only favicon/apple-touch icons in src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx, so no og:image is configured - the PR bodies were not read in full.
README claims about Clerk capabilities (passwordless, passkeys, MFA, impersonation, forgot/reset password, delete account) - these are Clerk dashboard settings, not verifiable from repo code.

Whether the live demo actually deploys on Vercel or Netlify: no vercel.json/netlify.toml exists and the README deploy section is platform-agnostic; only .gitignore and the /_vercel matcher hint at Vercel.
The paid Pro and Plus sibling products referenced by the upsell copy (their repos/features were not inspected - out of scope).
Dependency vulnerability state (`npm audit` / `npm audit signatures` runs in release.yml but was not run here) and the exact transitive origin of the pinned hono override (no install performed).
Language percentages come from GitHub's detector, which reports only TypeScript/CSS and ignores JSON/SQL/Markdown bytes in the repo.
Issue-quality and reviewer-latency metrics (time-to-first-response, stale PR age) were not computed; only open/closed counts and the 90-day commit count were measured.
